item.title: Weill Cornell Medicine receives ARPA-H award to advance lymphatic disease diagnosis
item.description: Weill Cornell Medicine has received a $5.2 million, initial two-year award from the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) Lymphatic Imaging, Genomics, and pHenotyping Technologies (LIGHT) program to develop a comprehensive and innovative approach to diagnosing lymphatic disease.

item.title: Machine learning enables prosthetic hands to control grip for daily tasks
item.description: Holding an egg requires a gentle touch. Squeeze too hard, and you'll make a mess. Opening a water bottle, on the other hand, needs a little more grip strength.

item.title: Researchers develop MRI-compatible polymer cables for safer medical brain stimulation
item.description: Anyone who has ever had to get a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan knows that magnetic and highly conductive materials are a no-go in the tube-shaped scanners.

item.title: EEG technology could be a useful tool for connecting brain signals with limb movements
item.description: People with from spinal cord injuries often lose some or all their limb function. In most patients, the nerves in their limbs work fine, and the neurons in their brain are still operational, but the damage to their spinal cords prevents the two areas from communicating.

item.title: Rice’s SynthX Center leads interdisciplinary effort to tackle rare lymphatic disorders
item.description: Rice University's SynthX Center, directed by Han Xiao, has received an up to five-year, $18 million award from the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) Lymphatic Imaging, Genomics and pHenotyping Technologies (LIGHT) program to develop innovative solutions for lymphatic diseases.

item.title: New AI framework mirrors human physiology to understand emotional experiences
item.description: Emotions are a fundamental part of human psychology-a complex process that has long distinguished us from machines.

item.title: Suppressing brain immune cells enhances memory recall in young mice
item.description: Babies of every species from mouse to human rapidly forget things that happen to them-an effect called infantile amnesia.

item.title: Severe vitamin D deficiency linked to higher hospitalizations for respiratory tract infections
item.description: Severe vitamin D deficiency is associated with a higher rate of hospitalization for respiratory tract infections such as bronchitis and pneumonia, according to a new study led by the University of Surrey.

item.title: Arthritis significantly restricts employment for millions of American adults
item.description: According to new research from the University of Delaware, nearly 40% of American adults ages 18 to 64 with arthritis - almost 10 million people - say the medical condition is limiting their ability to work.

item.title: UT Southwestern performs first regional whole-liver chemotherapy for rare eye cancer
item.description: A team at UT Southwestern Medical Center this week became the first in Texas and neighboring states to successfully perform a novel procedure to deliver whole-liver chemotherapy to treat metastatic uveal melanoma, a rare and deadly eye cancer.
